THE STATE OF MADHYA PRADESH THROUGH POLICE  S TAT I O N SIRMOUR DISTRICT REWA (MADHYA  PRADESH)
 .
 (BY SHRI NARENDRA CHOURASIA, GOVT. ADVOCATE)

This application coming on for admission this day, the   following:
 ORDER

This is the second bail application filed on behalf of the applicant/accused under Section 438 of the Cr.P.C. for grant of anticipatory bail, as he is under apprehension of his arrest, in connection with Crime No.38/2021, registered at Police Station Sirmour, District Rewa (M.P.) for the offences punishable under Sections 409, 420, 467, 468, 471, 120-B and 201 of Indian Penal Code and Sections 7C, 13(1)(a) and 13(2) of Prevention of Corruption Act.
2. Learned counsel appearing for the applicant submitted that applicant is innocent and has falsely been implicated in the case.
Applicant himself reported the incident of embezzlement and tried to lodge first information report against Computer Operator Harihar Prasad Patel.
A false complaint has been made by one Ramswamber Verma and applicant was given clean chit in his complaint.
Sanction has not been obtained for prosecuting the applicant.

Applicant is an old man aged about 64 Dayaram Mishra vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 13 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/116001084/
1 years with no criminal past and have a good reputation in society.

sentences.text: Appellant is ready to cooperate in investigation of case In these circumstances, applicant may be enlarged on anticipatory bail.
3. Learned Govt. Advocate appearing for the State opposed the application for grant of anticipatory bail.
It is submitted that applicant will be required for investigation in the case.
Earlier bail application filed by applicant was dismissed as withdrawn as he was not having a good case.
There is no change in circumstances thereafter, therefore, repeat bail application for grant of anticipatory bail may be dismissed.

4. Heard the learned counsel for the parties.
5.
Perused the case diary.

6. On perusal of case diary it is found that beneficiaries namely Kripashanker Mishra, Ajay Pandey,
Premwati Kol, Rohit Rawat, Pushpraj Rawat have given statement to police that applicant Dayaram Mishra and Harihar Prasad Patel had credited into their account 3rd installment under Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana without their consent and thereafter they took the said money from them.
Applicant is said to have credited an amount of Rs.1-1 Lakh each in account of ineligible beneficiaries.

Applicant Dayaram Mishra and President of Nagar Parishad Shanti Chourasia and Operator Harihar Prasad Patel has deposited Rs.One Lakh - Rs.Two Lakhs as 3rd instalment in account of beneficiaries namely Sukhlal Kol, Surendra Prasad Mishra, Rambhajan Kol, Chandrawati Saket, Umesh Kumar Soni, Rajbahoran Kushwaha, Dadan Prasad Sen, Badku Kol, Rajau Kol,
Ramvishal, Sarman Saket, Sukhlal, Shanker, Premwati, Rajkumar, Tulsa, Pushpraj Adiwasi,
Ramsiya, Kamta Prasad Tiwari and Rajmani Napit.
As per policy 3rd installment is to be of Rs.50000/- only and they had taken back Rs.One Lakh from beneficiaries.
Prima facie offence appears to be made out against the applicant.
Applicant will be required for investigation of the case.
7. In view of aforesaid, repeat application for grant of anticipatory bail to applicant is dismissed.

(VISHAL DHAGAT) JUDGE mms Dayaram Mishra vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 13 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/116001084/
